newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurostocks mixed ahead of US inflation data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurostocks mixed ahead of US inflation data.

text.p: European stocks were mixed in cautious early trade on Tuesday with investors keeping a wary eye open for U.S. inflation figures due later in the day for pointers on the direction of interest rates.
In foreign exchanges, the dollar strengthened against the the mark, which was still suffering from worries over a soft single European currency, but was largely unchanged on the yen.

London, which set three closing records last week, edged modestly higher after dropping nearly one percent on Monday. Investors were still jittery over what the country's budget has in store next month.

"We're only three weeks away from the budget now and I think the market will continue to be nervous," said one trader. "We still look vulnerable to more profit-taking because there's a lot of profits to be taken."

The leading FTSE -100 index was up 0.25 percent at one point but dealings were thin. Wall Street, which ended in the red overnight after a six-day record-breaking run last week, provided no encouragement.
The London market was expected to remain edgy after reports on Monday that the government could cut valuable tax breaks for pension funds in the July 2 budget.
"It looks like the tax credit will go," said one trader. "It's just too tempting a target for the government to resist, and if it does then the market should go down quite a bit more."
British government bonds were steady as the market absorbed the implications of the Amsterdam EU summit's approval of the budget stability pact and a resolution on boosting employment and growth.
In Frankfurt, floor trade fell with Monday's drop on Wall Street removing the impetus for some of the recent gains. The DAX index was down 0.47 percent.
"There is a lot of nervousness around and a lot of it is related to the negotiations at the Amsterdam summit," said one trader of the European Union summit.
"A lot of the agreements in Amsterdam are being seen as posturing. It's all politics, and everyone thinks they are just trying to paper over the cracks," the trader said.

Paris, which saw volatile trading on Monday after touching a trading peak, slipped into the minus column amid nerves over the data on U.S. consumer prices for May which will give clues on the state of the American economy and prospects for interest rates.
In currencies, the dollar climbed by nearly a pfennig to

1.7363 marks with the German currency under pressure and the dollar benefiting from its safe haven reputation as the stability pact improved prospects for the launch of a soft European single currency.

But the U.S. currency was fighting to hold its gains on the yen as traders focused their attention on this week's Japanese May trade data, expected to show a growing surplus, and U.S. April figures, where a worsening deficit, is expected.

Anticipation of the data has added piquancy to expectations of the Group of Seven industrial nations meeting in Denver on June 20-22. The market fears that the expanding trade gap will see sparks fly between the U.S. and Japan.
Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered, said the U.S. was indeed concerned about trade but not to the point that they were willing to engage heavily in exchange rate rhetoric.
"The issue is to try to get Japan to boost demand and how they do that, rather than by trying to engineer a manipulation of exchange rates," said Fox.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7363 marks and 113.49 yen, compared with 1.7291 and 113.39 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 2.5 points at 4747.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 9.01 points at 2786.86.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 17.82 points at 3747.29.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $341.40 an ounce, compared with Monday's close of $341.75. Silver was unchanged at $4.72.
